paragraphs: Bab 27, as indicated by the M II table of contents, was to provide a catalogue of scriptural loci that suggest — at least on a plain reading — divine corporeality, likeness, and visibility. These would include: - The image-of-God language (Gen 1:26, "Let us make man in our image, after our likeness"; Gen 1:27, "God created man in His own image"; Gen 5:1; Gen 9:6). - Bodily-organ language (the eyes, ears, mouth, hands, arm, fingers, feet, heart of God). - Bodily-act language (God's coming, going, standing, sitting, walking, riding). - Emotional language (God's anger, vengeance, jealousy, joy, repentance, regret). - Visual-encounter language (Isa 6:1, "I saw the Lord sitting on a throne"; Exod 24:10, "they saw the God of Israel"; Num 12:8, "mouth to mouth I speak to him"). - Localized-presence language (the divine kingship in heaven; the divine presence on Mount Sinai; the divine descent on the Tabernacle and Temple). The bab functions as the survey that the next bab (Bab 28) will refute — i.e., demonstrate that all of these passages are to be read by taʾwīl (figurative interpretation), not by plain literalism. In the surviving Cairo text, the bab is folded into the opening of Bab 28 (treated below). Bab 28 §§1–16 systematically addresses each major category of anthropomorphic-suggestive language and provides its non-literal interpretation. The catalogue function of Bab 27 is therefore effectively integrated with the rebuttal of Bab 28. ---
